resources.string: Editor unavailable. Tap the text field and try again.
Enable ReteKey, then type in the field to try the keyboard.
How solid the floating panel is. Lower lets more of the app show through.

Tick the layouts the layout key at the bottom right should walk through, and order them with ▲ ▼. That key is captioned with where it goes next — QWE, 2BS — in bold capitals, and holding it opens the menu page.
How much of the screen\'s height the keyboard takes, from 1% to 50%. The menu page\'s size keys move it too, two points at a time.
A strip above the keys for the things that are not letters: selecting, the clipboard, moving the cursor, text of your own, key combinations you assemble. It has a screen of its own.
The strip above the keys. Drag a row by its ≡ handle to order it, ▲ ▼ to nudge, ✕ to take it off. Tap a text or key-combination row to edit it.
Built-in actions you have not put on it. ＋ adds one to the end.
A tap sends it once. Holding presses the key and leaves it down until you press the slot again — that is how Shift stays held for a selection.

Many phones draw hide-keyboard and switch-keyboard buttons under an open keyboard, and a keyboard that ignores them puts its bottom row where it cannot be pressed. Automatic keeps that strip only where the system is actually using it.
Hanja and code-point panels follow the keyboard: above it when it is docked, in its place when it floats
Monochrome: black and white keys with an outline, for E-Ink screens
Light or dark, for the keyboard and for these screens. On Android 12 and later the colours are taken from the system\'s own palette, so the keyboard matches the wallpaper theme you have set.
Use the floating keyboard on this screen

Which layout a plugged-in or Bluetooth keyboard follows while a layout is on the screen. They need not match: you can type Dvorak on the screen and Colemak on the keys. Only layouts with more than one physical form are listed — Korean has one, 2벌식, which 천지인 and 나랏글 already use.
Keyboard height and the floating panel, as they are for a screen held upright. The layouts for this screen have a page of their own.
Keyboard height and the floating panel, as they are for a screen held sideways. The layouts for this screen have a page of their own.
Which layouts the layout key walks through, and their order, for a screen held upright.
Which layouts the layout key walks through, and their order, for a screen held sideways.
Set the strength of each; drag a slider to 0 to turn it off.

A terminal cannot underline a syllable while you build it. Either the keyboard shows it on its own strip and sends it when it closes, or it is typed into the terminal and taken back with every stroke.
Show the syllable on the keyboard\'s strip
Holding a key repeats it — space, enter, backspace, and the arrow keys. Keys that hold an alternate character type that instead.

Register physical keys for the KO/EN toggle, the Hanja key and Unicode entry on a Bluetooth or wired keyboard. Each function can have several. Shift+Space and a keyboard\'s own 한/영 and 한자 keys are registered already, with Ctrl+Shift+U for Unicode entry; remove any of them and it stays removed.
Press the shortcut… (the whole combination is taken; a modifier on its own registers itself; tap here or press Back to cancel)
A registered Unicode key opens U+ entry: type the hex digits and Enter puts the character in. The menu page\'s Uni key does the same with no hardware keyboard attached.
A registered Hanja key converts the selection, or the reading before the cursor, to Hanja.
한자 키 인식됨 — 변환 기능은 준비 중입니다.
A terminal has no selection to copy or cut.

The box that shows what you just typed, over the keyboard. A finger covers the key it presses, which is why it is there — but it is a box over the keys, so it can be turned off, and made see-through enough to read the row underneath.
No motion: nothing flashes, shades or pops up when a key is pressed (also on when Android\'s \"Remove animations\" is on)
Show what was typed over the keyboard

The keyboard reads Android\'s clipboard when it comes up, so what you copied elsewhere is already in the Clip list. Turn that off and it never looks: text then reaches the keyboard only by being shared into it.
Share text to ReteKey from any app\'s Share menu and it is kept here, never on the system clipboard. Tap it in the Clip list to type it. How long it is kept:
Layout installed: %1$s. Turn it on in settings.
That layout file could not be read.
This replaces the layout you have installed: %1$s
This file does not begin with the layout header.
This layout is written for a later version of ReteKey.
This file is far larger than a layout.
One of the keys types more characters than a key can.
One of the rows has no keys in it.
A layout needs three rows of keys.

A layout is text: three rows of keys, with what each key holds after a bar. Install one by sharing it to Install a ReteKey layout, or by opening a .rkl file — one at a time, and the new one replaces the old.
A whole layout, to copy and change. Lines this version does not know are ignored, so a file written for a later one still works:
Kept in ReteKey — the clipboard was not touched.
Clipboard too long — pasted the first part only.
